title: Simple sorting and checking the result
goal: Sort an array copy by selection and check order, length and repeated values.

prerequisites.text: Pass an array with its length, traverse valid indices and find the minimum of a nonempty range.

terms.title: Sorted prefix
terms.definition: The initial part of the array before index next. It is already ordered and contains the smallest values.

terms.title: Swap
terms.definition: An exchange of two values using a temporary variable. The array keeps the same values and their counts.

terms.title: Multiplicity
terms.definition: The number of occurrences of a value. Equal values are counted individually.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: Measurements are recorded in time order. A report needs a separate row in ascending order. Keep the original log and rearrange the values in a copy.
Selection sort puts the next minimum at index next. Values to its right still need to be ordered. Before the first pass, the sorted part is empty.
The result has two observable properties. Adjacent values appear in nondecreasing order. Each value occurs as many times as it does in the original row.

sections.title: Sorting four readings
paragraphs: Trace the sorting of 4, 1, 4, 2. On each pass, find the index of the minimum in the remaining range and exchange the two elements using saved. One element joins the sorted part after each pass.
steps: At next = 0, the minimum 1 is at index 1. The swap puts 1 at the front.
At next = 1, the last value, 2, is the minimum of the rest. The swap puts it at index 1.
At next = 2, the remaining values are equal. The final row 1 2 4 4 contains two fours.

sections.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: The condition next + 1 < length leaves at least one later element to search. At lengths 0 and 1, the outer loop runs zero times. Length is limited to eight, so adding one fits in int.
With the unsigned type size_t, length - 1 at length zero gives a large value. Check the length before subtracting. The loop shown uses no subtraction.
Clang rejects sorted = original in the diagnostic snippet. With two arrays already declared, copy elements by index from 0 through length minus one.

sections.title: Apply the idea
paragraphs: The worked example rearranges the displayed readings in place. The practice task stores the original row in a separate array and gives its copy to the sorting function.
For the input row 3, -1, 3, 2, the row -1 2 3 9 is already ordered. Comparing frequencies reveals that the second 3 has been replaced by 9.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Sort an array copy by selection and check order, length and repeated values.

selfcheck.prompt: What is the row 4, 1, 4, 2 immediately after the pass with next = 0?
feedback: The first swap exchanges only 4 and 1.
That result needs another pass to place 2 at index 1.
The first pass selects the smallest value and puts it at the front.

selfcheck.prompt: Why is -1 2 3 9 incorrect for the original 3, -1, 3, 2?
feedback: The order is correct. Compare how often each value occurs.
The values have changed even though the order and length are correct.
The lengths match, but a value can still have been replaced.

selfcheck.prompt: How many times does the outer loop execute at length 1?
feedback: At next = 0, 1 < 1 is false. The sole element is already in place.
The first condition is checked before the loop body.
A single element offers no pair to swap.

selfcheck.prompt: For 2, -2, 2, 0, -2, write the sorted row and describe two checks that catch a lost repeat or a wrongly ordered pair.
selfcheck.feedback: The answer is -2 -2 0 2 2. Compare every adjacent pair. Verify that -2, 0 and 2 occur as often as in the original, including both occurrences of -2 and of 2.

practice.title: A reading report with a sorted copy
practice.task: On the first line, enter the length from 0 to 8. At 0, print the single line empty. Otherwise enter one integer from -99 to 99 on each of the following lines. Print the original values separated by spaces on the first output line and the sorted copy on the second. Print invalid for an invalid length or a missing or invalid required value. The program ignores any lines after the required inputs. The starter already handles reading, copying by index and printing.
practice.hint: The inner loop updates least. Its comparison should leave least at the index of the smallest value inspected within the remaining range.
criteria: For four readings 3, -1, 3, 2, the first output line stays 3 -1 3 2 and the second is -1 2 3 3.
Use the second line to check adjacent order and compare each value's frequency with the first line.
At length 1, the two lines match. At length 0, the output is just empty.
Test the maximum length, an already sorted sequence and invalid input.

cases.label: Extra character on a reading line

steps.action: Run the starter with the prefilled input and compare the two lines.
steps.why: The order on the second line reveals what the inner loop selects.
steps.expected: The original row stays 3 -1 3 2. The starter gives 3 3 2 -1 as the copy, with larger values first.

steps.action: Fix the choice of the next value in sort_ascending and run again.
steps.why: Each pass should put the smallest remaining value at index next.
steps.expected: The second line is -1 2 3 3. The first line stays the same.

steps.action: Try lengths 0, 1, 2 and 8. Compare how often repeated values occur in the two lines.
steps.why: Short cases show when swaps are needed. Repeats show that swapping preserves the collection of values.
steps.expected: Length 0 prints empty and length 1 prints two identical rows. Two values in reverse order need one swap.

exercises.title: Check order and membership yourself
exercises.task: Enter the lines 5, 2, -2, 2, 0, -2. Write the expected lines, then compare adjacent order and the number of occurrences of each value with the output.
criteria: Both lines contain two values of -2, one zero and two values of 2.
